flagged.evidence: The item defines dyadic intervals as having dyadic-rational endpoints, but Proof 1.1 instructs: “center a dyadic interval of width at most 2^{-q} at its rational output.” A valid Cauchy query may return a non-dyadic rational such as 1/3; the midpoint of two dyadic endpoints is dyadic, so such an interval cannot be centered exactly at that output. Rounding the output to a dyadic rational and widening the interval would close this local construction gap.
